CUSTOM:web_search.description:
One resolved search. `links` are the bare result URLs in rank order;
`results` carries the per-result metadata the card renders — title, snippet,
and whatever else the backend for that `kind` returns — so the sources show
as titled rows rather than naked URLs.
CUSTOM:web_search.title: WebSearchEvent

ExternalOutputAction.description:
One real-world side effect a connector write-tool performed during a run —
a sent email, a created Notion page, etc. Powers one row of the FE
ExternalOutputCard ("Done in the world").

`view_url` is best-effort: present only when the tool response carried a
resolvable link to the created/affected resource. When absent the FE simply
renders no "View" button. There is deliberately no `undo` — most external
writes (a sent email, a posted message) cannot be reversed, so the 5s undo
countdown is a FE-only affordance the backend never promises.
ExternalOutputAction.title: ExternalOutputAction

CUSTOM:external_output.description:
Emitted once at plan completion summarizing every external write a run
performed. Maps to the FE ExternalOutputCard; empty `actions` means the run
only read/produced artifacts and the card is not shown.
CUSTOM:external_output.title: ExternalOutputEvent

CUSTOM:memory_updated.description:
Emitted when user_memory or project_memory has been replaced by an LLM
tool call. `scope` is 'user' or 'project'; `scope_id` is the auth0_id or
project_id (as string). `version` is the new opaque CAS counter.
CUSTOM:memory_updated.title: MemoryUpdatedEvent

CUSTOM:tool_connect_prompt.description:
The model called a connector tool for an app the user hasn't linked.
The UI renders a 'Connect <App>' button; clicking it opens the OAuth or
API-key flow while the tool call waits. If the user declines/dismisses,
POST ``{"response": "cancel"}`` to ``respond_url`` so the backend returns
that outcome to the model in the same turn.
CUSTOM:tool_connect_prompt.title: ToolConnectPromptEvent

CUSTOM:user_prompt.description:
Generic mid-stream "the model is asking the user something" event.

The same event handles connector permission asks, plan approvals,
destructive-action confirmations, and free-text clarifications.
Backend code calls `core.prompt_gate.ask_user(...)` which emits this
event and blocks until the FE POSTs to `respond_url`.

Fields:
  prompt_id    — UUID; FE POSTs to /chats/prompts/{prompt_id}.
  kind         — "permission" | "confirm" | "choice" | "input".
  title        — headline rendered in the assistant message.
  description  — optional longer body.
  options      — for choice-style kinds, [{value, label, style?}].
  metadata     — kind-specific context (e.g. {connector_slug, tool_slug,
                 suggested_args} for permission asks). FE renders or
                 ignores per its UI.
  respond_url  — server-built path to POST the response to.
CUSTOM:user_prompt.title: UserPromptEvent

CUSTOM:question_prompt.description:
The assistant is asking the user one or more clarifying questions.

Dedicated, fully-typed replacement for `user_prompt` kind=questions.
Resolve by POSTing to `respond_url` with
`{"response": {"answers": {question_id: value}}}`.
CUSTOM:question_prompt.title: QuestionPromptEvent

CUSTOM:permission_prompt.description:
The backend paused an exact connector call whose binary permission is
undecided. The model never handles this decision.

Resolve by POSTing to `respond_url` with
`{"response": "allow" | "allow_once" | "block"}` (a plain string).
CUSTOM:permission_prompt.title: PermissionPromptEvent

CUSTOM:approval_prompt.description:
A plan node is about to perform an external write (send an email, post to
LinkedIn, create a record, …) and the run is paused until the user approves.

Connector calls use `permission_prompt` as their only approval. This event
remains for non-connector actions that still need a dedicated confirmation.

`preview_xml` is a renderable draft of what will be sent — an `<email>` block
(to/subject/body) or a `<post>` block — built the same way the chat path emits
`<chart>`/table XML. The FE renders it as an editable/preview card alongside
the approve/reject buttons; empty when the action has no natural preview.

Resolve by POSTing to `respond_url` with
`{"response": "approve" | "approve_all" | "reject"}` (a plain string).
CUSTOM:approval_prompt.title: ApprovalPromptEvent

CUSTOM:stream_heartbeat.description: Keepalive emitted while a long-running tool leaves the stream idle.
CUSTOM:stream_heartbeat.title: StreamHeartbeatEvent

get.description:
Resume and expose the browser owned by this user and chat.

Readable shares deliberately do not inherit the owner's logged-in browser:
that sandbox can contain authenticated accounts and cookies. Matching the
write-side owner check keeps those credentials scoped to their owner.

Generic responder for mid-stream `user_prompt` SSE events.

Wakes the backend coroutine that's blocked on this prompt_id. The
same endpoint handles connector permission asks today, plan
approvals / confirmations / free-text clarifications tomorrow — the
`kind` in the originating SSE event tells the FE how to render.

post.description:
Generate a starting system instruction, sound, and tags from a persona's
name + description. Nothing is saved — the FE uses this to seed the editor.

Stream advice on improving a draft persona. The FE sends the current
editor state (the version being edited); all saved versions of the repo are
pulled in as context. The draft persona need not be saved.

matching the connector's `api_key_fields` and submits them in

OrganizationRole.title: OrganizationRole
OrganizationRole.description:
A user's org-wide standing. `owner` bought the org — full control
including plans, credit purchases, invoices, and card changes; exactly one
per org. `admin` manages the workspace but cannot mutate billing or payment
state. `member` is the baseline: their actual access comes from ProjectMember
grant rows. `service` is a machine principal for someone who
reached us through a surface without ever signing up — a Slack member
talking to the bot. It spends the owner's wallet the way an admin does, and
holds no powers at all: resolve_role sends it down the grant path, where it
has no grants.

A bare person reference — project members and org members alike; the
grant table a row came from already says what they are.
